prompt:
Compute absolute Spearman rank correlations between columns 2 to 8 and columns 9 to 17 and run a two-sided, p < 0.05 significance test on the correlations without correcting for multiple comparisons. Exclude subjects that appear to induce spurious correlations. Plot significant correlations in a matrix using the `plot_correlation_matrix` tool.

DATASET: correlates_common_subjects
  386 subjects. Symptoms + task measures only. Subject-level.
  386 rows, 386 subjects (1.0 rows per subject, subject-level)
  columns 2-8  (symptoms): 7-up, 7-down, GAD-7, BIS, BAS, SHAPS, PSWQ
  columns 9-17 (measures): Acc, Pts, WS, LS, Pers, beta, eta_p, eta_n, kappa
  63 correlations, uncorrected at alpha=0.05 -> ~3.2 false positives expected from noise alone

SUPPORTING TABLES (evidence for deciding who to exclude; they are NOT part of the correlation):
  survey_data: 406 subjects x per-item survey responses plus per-scale response times.
    406 rows, 60 columns, 406 subjects; columns: subject, gad7_q01, gad7_q02, gad7_q03, gad7_q04, gad7_q05, gad7_q06, gad7_q07, gad7_q08, gad7_rt ...

WHAT THE COLUMNS MEAN:
  7-up           7 Up mania/hypomania screen (higher = more symptoms)
  7-down         7 Down depression screen (higher = more symptoms)
  GAD-7          Generalised Anxiety Disorder 7-item scale
  BIS            Behavioural Inhibition System sensitivity
  BAS            Behavioural Activation System sensitivity
  SHAPS          Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (anhedonia)
  PSWQ           Penn State Worry Questionnaire
  Acc            proportion of correct choices in the reversal-learning task
  Pts            total points earned
  WS             win-stay rate: P(repeat choice | previous trial rewarded)
  LS             lose-shift rate: P(switch choice | previous trial unrewarded)
  Pers           perseveration: repeated choices after contingency reversal
  beta           inverse temperature from the RL model (choice determinism)
  eta_p          learning rate for positive prediction errors
  eta_n          learning rate for negative prediction errors
  kappa          choice-stickiness parameter

trace.thought: Identify subjects who induce spurious correlations to exclude them before correlation analysis.

trace.thought: Compute absolute Spearman correlations between symptom and task measure columns excluding careless subjects, with uncorrected p<0.05 significance test.
Plot significant absolute Spearman correlations between symptom scales and task measures with uncorrected p<0.05 after excluding careless subjects.

outcome.final_claim: There are 25 significant absolute Spearman correlations (p < 0.05, uncorrected) between symptom scales (columns 2-8) and task measures (columns 9-17) in the correlates_common_subjects dataset after excluding 41 subjects flagged for careless responding based on straightlining. The strongest correlations include negative associations between 7-up mania/hypomania symptoms and inverse temperature (beta, rho = -0.3794), win-stay rate (WS, rho = -0.3268), accuracy (Acc, rho = -0.295), and others. Some weaker but significant correlations involve BIS, 7-down depression, GAD-7 anxiety, and PSWQ worry scales with various task measures. About 3.2 false positives are expected by chance given 63 tests, so some findings may be noise. The correlation matrix plot visually highlights these significant correlations.
limitations: Robustness of these correlations to different quality control policies (e.g., weighted inclusion, hard thresholding) is unknown.
Whether these associations replicate in an independent sample with different symptom scales and task measures is unknown.
Correction for multiple comparisons was not applied, so which findings survive stringent control is unclear.
outcome.resolving_measurement: Testing associations under multiple selection policies and checking replication in an independent sample with matched constructs, as well as applying multiple comparison correction.
